headline: Minor boy tortured to death in Hardoi
author: Pervez Iqbal Siddiqui
description: LUCKNOW: In a barbaric incident, a minor boy was given electric shocks, hanged upside down from the ceiling, his vital parts hit by batons and hot wat
body_text: LUCKNOW: In a barbaric incident, a minor boy was given electric shocks, hanged upside down from the ceiling, his vital parts hit by batons and hot water forced down his nostrils for four days till he finally breathed his last in Hardoi on June 23. And the Hardoi police were worse. Conniving with a Samajwadi Party ex-MLA, his son and their two associates who allegedly killed the boy during interrogation for a missing countrymade pistol, the Hardoi police dismissed the murder as a cholera death. And this despite evident superficial injuries on the body being testimony to the agony and pain the boy underwent before death. Leave alone lodging a criminal case against the politician and his associates, the police allegedly joined hands with them to hound out the boy's family members from their native village. And till date the family is on its toes seeking justice. In the wee hours of June 23, Shiv Narain, a paan shop owner of Azad Nagar locality in Madhoganj police circle of Hardoi, was informed by a local youth that his son Nirmal had died. Shiv and his wife Somwati rushed to the tea stall where Nirmal's body was lying. They found superficial injury marks on Nirmal's body and realised that their fears had turned out to be true. Nirmal was working as a domestic help in the house of former SP MLA Dharmagya Misra. On June 19, Misra's son Anurag found his illicit countrymade pistol missing from his room and doubting Nirmal's involvement in the incident, assaulted the boy brutally. Another domestic help who was a witness to Nirmal being assaulted, informed Shiv, who in turn rushed to rescue his son. He was, however, thrown out of the house allegedly by Anurag and his musclemen. Terrified, Shiv, his wife and their two sons Sandeep (10) and Rahul (8) remained confined to their house for four days praying for Nirmal's safety. However Nirmal was eventually killed allegedly by the politician, his son and others. Interestingly the Madhoganj police, on being approached by Shiv, termed the incident as one of cholera death. They also refused to send the body for post-mortem examination and released it after a 'panchnama'. "But some local residents helped me meet senior police officials in the state capital,� Shiv told TNN on Sunday. Finally the body was sent for post-mortem examination which corroborated the allegations that the victim was electrocuted. Burn and fracture injuries on his body and vital parts were also found. Not left with much choice, the police lodged a murder case on the basis of autopsy report but refused to name the politician even as a suspect, leave alone an accused. DIG (Lucknow range) AKD Dwivedi confirmed the sequence of events as narrated by Shiv, adding that action was being initiated.
